advances: The fixed-origin height rule fails even with an actual equal-critical cover and affine cancellation. This family has normalized depth 13/36 and only supplies a counterexample to the proposed height cancellation.

proof:
Use the unsheared product in ba7d50004292d433 with continuous triangle $T$ and centroid zero. Its three caps are given by $\lambda_i(x)-1/3+\ell_i(p)\ge0$ with $\lambda_i(x)=(1+u_i\cdot x)/3$. Changing the coefficient of $\ell_i$ from $3$ to $10$ after multiplying the margin by $3$ leaves every sampled trace identical: $\ell_i(p_i)=2$, $\ell_i(p_j)=-1$ for $j\ne i$, and $-1\le u_i\cdot x\le2$ on $T$. The shear $(p,x)\mapsto(p,x+b(p))$ maps closed halfspaces bijectively and translates every individual fiber, so the positive lattice census, actual maximum depth and deepest mark remain as in that fact. The new three margins sum to zero, and their proper sections are precisely the central lines $u_i\cdot x=0$ intersected with $T$. For $u_i=e_1,e_2$ the section length is $2$, and for $u_i=-e_1-e_2$ it is $2\sqrt2$. Each segment is centered at zero, and division by $\|u_i\|$ gives coarea $2$.

Write $L_f$ for the arclength of an edge of $T$ and $x_f(t)$ for its affine parametrization, $0\le t\le1$. On every outer edge $W=1/3$ and the charge per arclength is $-1/36$. On the central edge it is $-1/36$ on the outer thirds and $11/36$ on the middle third, since exactly one or two of the three barycentric caps cover those parts respectively. Thus the charge divided by $L_f$ is the sum of the central density $w=-1/9,2/9,-1/9$ on the thirds and the measure
$$
\frac1{12}\int_0^1\left[\delta_{(0,x_f(t))}-\frac13\sum_{j=1}^3\delta_{(p_j,x_f(t)+b(p_j))}\right]\,dt .
$$
The central density integrates nonnegatively against a concave function $f(t)$ since $2f(t)\ge f(t-1/3)+f(t+1/3)$ on the middle third. The second term integrates nonnegatively by Jensen since the central point is the average of the three outer points. Apply the two signs of an affine test to conclude affine annihilation.

The unnormalized outward edge normals are $v_f=-e_1,-e_2,e_1+e_2$, each with support value $1$ and $L_f/\|v_f\|=3$. At base $p$ the fixed height is $(1+v_f\cdot b(p))/\|v_f\|>0$ and the moving height is $1/\|v_f\|$. On the edge with $v_f=e_1+e_2$, the central charge has mass $L_f/12$, and the three outer charges each have mass $-L_f/36$. After height multiplication these still sum to zero since $\sum_j b(p_j)=0$. The base first moment becomes $-(\epsilon/12)\sum_j(p_j)_1p_j=-(\epsilon/12)(2,1)$. For the horizontal second divergences of these finite measures, test an affine function multiplied by a smooth cutoff equal to one on a neighborhood of the compact supports. The second derivative vanishes on the supports. The corresponding affine moments of the anchored Jensen charges vanish by their barycenter identities. A constant change of reference origin would only subtract a constant times the original charge on this normal and would leave the first moment unchanged.

The normal-summed difference has no central component and on each outer fiber equals $-(b(p_j)\cdot n)dS_{\partial K_{p_j}}/36$. Fiberwise Gauss–Green gives
$$
D=\frac1{36}\operatorname{div}_x\left(\sum_{j=1}^3 b(p_j)\mathbf1_{K_{p_j}}\,dx\right),
$$
where the summands are marked with their bases. Tests constant in $x$ integrate to zero. The continuous first moment is $-V\sum_j b(p_j)/36=0$. For the tests $(z_1\pm x_1)^2$, use $\partial_{x_1}= \pm2(z_1\pm x_1)$ on those functions, the centroid $b(p_j)$ of the translated fiber and $\sum_j(p_j)_1^2=2$. This gives the two displayed values, respectively $-5/32$ and $3/32$ at $\epsilon=1/4$.

For a proper cut $u\cdot x\ge s$ in one fiber and a smooth test $f$, apply Gauss–Green on the retained fiber to $f(x)(x-c)$, where $c$ is its chosen reference point. The old-boundary flux equals the retained bulk integral of $2f+(x-c)\cdot\nabla f$ plus $(s-u\cdot c)/\|u\|$ times the section integral of $f$, because the new section normal is $-u/\|u\|$. In this example each proper section has $p=0$, $s=0$ and both reference points zero there. Full or empty outer traces have no section terms. At $f=1$, the weighted sum of retained bulk integrals minus $\beta$ times the full bulk integral is $2(13V/9-\beta(4V))=0$ for either reference. For nonconstant tests the bulk gradient term is still present, as the two values of $D$ exhibit.

statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}\{(2,-1),(-1,2),(-1,-1)\}$, $V=9/2$ and $P=\{0,p_1,p_2,p_3\}$ with $p_1=(1,0)$, $p_2=(0,1)$ and $p_3=(-1,-1)$. For $0<\epsilon<1$, write a variable base as $z=(z_1,z_2)$ and put $b(z)=\epsilon z_1 e_1$. Use the lattice-complete sheared product with fibers $K_p=T+b(p)$ and actual closed caps
$$
H_i=\{(z,x):10\ell_i(z)+u_i\cdot(x-b(z))\ge0\},\qquad
\ell=(2z_1-z_2,2z_2-z_1,-z_1-z_2),\quad
(u_1,u_2,u_3)=(e_1,e_2,-e_1-e_2).
$$
They cover the ambient space, are critical at $(0,0)$ with each mixed area $13V/9$, and have normalized common depth $\beta=13/36$. Each has just one proper section, at the central fiber, with physical centroid $(0,0)$ and coarea $2$ for the displayed margin. For $W=\frac13\sum_i\mathbf1_{H_i}$ let $\sigma=(W-\beta)\sum_{p\in P}dS_{\partial K_p}$ with each outward unit continuous normal $n$ retained as a mark. At each normal, $\sigma$ integrates nonnegatively against every continuous concave roof on the convex hull of the corresponding lifted edges and annihilates every affine physical test.

Let $h_{\rm fixed}=x\cdot n$ and $h_{\rm move}=(x-b(p))\cdot n$. Both heights are positive. At $n=(1,1)/\sqrt2$, the part of $h_{\rm fixed}\sigma$ has zero mass and base first moment $-(\epsilon/12)(2,1)$. In particular this part cannot be a sum solely of horizontal second divergences of finite matrix-valued measures supported on the compact lifted faces and finitely many anchored Jensen charges with finite first moments. When the normal labels are summed out, $D=(h_{\rm fixed}-h_{\rm move})\sigma$ has zero mass and all physical first moments zero, but
$$
\int (z_1+x_1)^2\,dD=-V\epsilon(1+\epsilon)/9,\qquad
\int (z_1-x_1)^2\,dD=V\epsilon(1-\epsilon)/9 .
$$
In this example all proper section-height terms in the cap divergence identity vanish for both height choices and every smooth test. The summed height-weighted scalar charge is zero for both choices.
title: A nonzero height residue for a balanced actual critical cap cover
